suggestions.title: openTarget's bare catch turns any error from the token lookup into a 409 'reconnect GitHub'
suggestions.failurePath: openGithubToken does two things: it runs a SQLite select (getRow) and then calls box.open. The `catch {}` at lines 107-115 catches everything, not only SecretBoxError. Example: the github_connection select throws a better-sqlite3 error such as SQLITE_BUSY or a schema error. The caller (chief model or MCP client) then gets 409 'the stored token does not decrypt; reconnect GitHub'. The connection is fine and reconnecting will not help. The real error is hidden. Because 409 is a 4xx, the daemon relay also does not retry what may be a transient error. Narrow it to `catch (err) { if (!(err instanceof SecretBoxError)) throw err; ... }` (SecretBoxError is in lib/secret-box.ts) so other errors keep their own status.
suggestions.evidence: github-reads.ts:107-115 `try { token = openGithubToken({ db: deps.db, box: deps.box }, teamId); } catch { throw new HttpError(409, 'github connection cannot be read (the stored token does not decrypt); reconnect GitHub'); }`. github-connection.ts:58-61 openGithubToken = getRow(db select) then deps.box.open(...). secret-box.ts:17 defines SecretBoxError, the only error the 409 message describes.

suggestions.title: No test checks the timeout value actually given to the GitHub fetch (6 s, under the 10 s relay timeout)
suggestions.evidence: Test '6 超时值低于 daemon relay 超时，fetch 拿到 AbortSignal' (apps/server/test/github-reads.test.ts:894-910) reads the number from the error message, which is built from the GITHUB_READ_TIMEOUT_MS constant (github-reads.ts:124). It also checks that some AbortSignal was passed. The lib test (lines 983-1006) calls githubList* directly with timeoutMs 50, so it never touches the value the service passes. I replaced line 199 `const timeoutMs = GITHUB_READ_TIMEOUT_MS;` with `GITHUB_READ_TIMEOUT_MS * 10` and ran github-reads, mcp-face, shared chief-tools and daemon claude-t4-tools: 79/79 pass. Mutation M20 in p5a2-mutations.txt changes the constant itself, so it moves the message and the signal together and does not cover this split. Related: a TimeoutError thrown while reading the body (lib/github.ts:496) can be changed to report 'malformed' with no test failing.
suggestions.failurePath: Code at head is correct; this is a gap in what the tests hold. Suppose a later edit passes a timeout of 10 s or more to githubList* while the error text still says 6000ms. The daemon relay (REMOTE_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS 10 s) then gives up first and retries the replaySafe read while the server's first GitHub request is still running. That produces overlapping requests on the team token, which is the failure this rule exists to prevent, and every test stays green. Suggested fix: spy on AbortSignal.timeout, or record the value the hanging fetch receives, in a chief-face call, and assert it is at most REMOTE_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS minus 3000.

suggestions.title: Outside authors' issue/PR titles now reach the chief, which holds write tools and can turn tool output into its system prompt through save_memory
suggestions.failurePath: On a public repo, anyone can open an issue or a fork PR whose title contains instructions. The chief calls `issues`, and the cleaned title (up to 200 code points) arrives as a tool result. If the model follows it, it can call write tools such as connect_repo, set_secret or run_builds, or save_memory, whose content is inlined into the chief system prompt every turn. The code puts nothing into the system layer directly, so ADR 0021 D5 holds as written. The mitigations are the data note in the descriptions, format-character stripping and the length caps. The save_memory path is pre-existing and acknowledged in the PR's Risk section.
